comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
**Done, both triggers, one path.** `reload_config` is an ordinary action - rebindable, in the menu under View, on `cmd+shift+,` (Ghostty's own chord for the same job). A file watcher dispatches *that action* rather than being a second way in, which is what keeps "one action path" true of something nobody pressed. Written into architecture.md as a rule: something the app notices on its own is a trigger for an action, never a second implementation of it.

**The card's hard part - per-pane encoders - is done properly rather than skipped.** `PaneInput` now holds its encoder, keymap and settings behind one `RwLock`, and a reload replaces all of them in every attached pane. Every pane or none: the card was right that a window whose panes disagree depending on when each was opened is worse than needing a relaunch. `crates/muster-bridge/tests/typing_reload.rs` is the proof, and it is a real one - the pane is opened *before* the file changes and typed into *after*, and it was confirmed to fail (timeout waiting for `^[t`) with the rebuild stubbed out.

The lock is on the keystroke path, so it was measured: `input.encode` is indistinguishable from the same benchmark on the unchanged tree. One read guard per keystroke, and what comes out of it is owned or an `Arc` clone, so nothing is held across a send.

**What reload does not do: change which daemons are attached.** Read, noticed, reported, left for a relaunch - attaching and detaching on a save is a question about live sessions, and getting it wrong costs somebody their panes.

**A refusal changes nothing at all**, which matters more here than at launch: an editor that saves halfway through a thought must not leave a window running half a config. Verified in a real window - a misspelled key logged `config.reload.refused` naming it, the derived renderer config was left untouched, and the window carried on.

Three things found on the way:

- **The watcher must watch the directory, not the file.** Every editor saves by writing a temporary file and renaming it over the original, which replaces the inode - a watch on the file fires once, for the deletion, then watches something nothing will ever write to again. Verified by saving that way.
- **`ReadAppearance`'s own comment said "when it can change, it becomes an event", and now it can.** Both exist, and the split is between two moments rather than redundant: a launch needs the answer before the renderer is built and before any event loop runs, so it asks; a reload happens while the window is up, so the core tells it. Same for bindings.
- **Comparing the file's daemons against the *attached* ones was wrong** and shipped for about an hour. A config naming no daemons still ends up with one attached, because Muster starts its own - so every reload of a file that never mentioned a daemon reported a change. Caught by running it. It compares against the last-applied file now.

`DividerView.color` stopped being a `static let`, as the card's sibling predicted it would have to.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Every config key is read once at `Startup`: `apply_config` parses the file and hands the results to statics (`BINDINGS`, `PANE_INPUT`), and a pane's encoder is built from them at attach. So editing `config.toml` does nothing until the app restarts.

Acceptable while the file is small. Irritating during exactly the phase where somebody is tuning it, which is the daily-driving phase, and the phase Muster is in now.

The awkward part is not re-reading the file, it is what to do with what is already open. Bindings are easy - the menu is rebuilt from them. Typing settings are not: an encoder is built per pane at attach, so a reload either rebuilds every pane's encoder or leaves a window whose panes disagree depending on when each was opened. That second outcome is worse than needing a relaunch, and is why this was left alone rather than half-done.

Worth deciding: whether reload is a first-class action (rebindable, in the menu, dispatchable by the CLI) or something that happens when the file changes on disk. The first is honest about when it happens; the second is what people expect.
title: ♻️ Changing the config means relaunching
